standard.title: Locate, process and respond to information in texts
standard.description: locate and process information and ideas in a range of spoken, written and multimodal texts, and respond in different ways to suit purpose
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can locate and respond to key information in familiar texts and categorise it using graphic organisers (AC9LS4C03). They extract information from prepared texts. They have not yet researched independently across multiple sources, processed information for specific purposes, or compared ideas across imaginative texts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students locate and process information and ideas in a range of spoken, written and multimodal target language texts, and respond in ways suited to the purpose — including research, comparison, creative response and procedural tasks.

nodes.label: Researching and processing information across sources
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can research topics of interest across multiple target language sources, extracting and organising information for a specified purpose.
nodes.minimum_width: Research a topic using at least two sources and organise key information in an appropriate format.
nodes.typical_width: Research topics across varied source types — print, digital, spoken, multimodal; extract key points about life in target language communities; answer questions about researched content; extract procedural language; use graphic organisers suited to purpose; read texts about real-world situations to inform decisions.
wider: Research a topic across target language and English sources — compare what each includes and excludes, and explain what each perspective adds
Evaluate two target language sources on the same topic for reliability — identify which is more credible and explain why
nodes.hinge_reason: Independent multi-source research is the prerequisite for the evaluation and synthesis demands of subsequent bands. Students who can only process teacher-prepared texts cannot develop source evaluation and synthesis skills.

response_modes.reason: Research skills develop through varied source types and topic conditions. Each new source type builds a new strategy — varied conditions build transferable research capacity.

success_criteria: Locates and extracts information from at least two sources without direct teacher prompting
Organises information in a format appropriate to the research purpose

nodes.label: Responding to texts with personal reactions and comparisons
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can respond to target language texts in varied ways — expressing personal reactions, opinions and comparisons about characters, ideas and cultural elements.
nodes.minimum_width: Express a personal reaction to at least one text using target language evaluative language; produce at least one comparison across two texts or characters.
nodes.typical_width: Compare main characters, events and ideas across texts; discuss key messages and cultural elements; respond to artworks and images with opinions; respond to First Nations Australian authors' stories in the target language; respond to questions about characters, values and ideas.
wider: Produce a comparative written response identifying similarities and differences between two texts — using comparison language structures in the target language
Respond to a First Nations Australian cultural story — addressing both the story's content and its cultural significance

response_modes.reason: Evaluative and comparative response language develops through encountering varied texts and practising different response types. Students need a bank of evaluative and comparative expressions before they can respond genuinely.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Responding to First Nations Australian stories and culturally embedded texts in the target language is where text engagement becomes genuinely intercultural — building cultural literacy through authentic encounter.
success_criteria: Expresses a personal reaction to a text using evaluative language
Produces at least one comparison across two texts, characters or ideas

nodes.label: Adapting texts for new purposes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can adapt target language texts for new purposes or audiences — resequencing, adding elements, changing cultural setting or creating alternative versions.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce at least one text adaptation with at least two changed elements, suited to a different purpose or audience.
nodes.typical_width: Adapt texts by resequencing events, adding new elements or creating alternative endings; change cultural setting to a different target language community context; create versions of texts suited to different audiences; produce adapted texts for real purposes.
wider: Create an adaptation that moves a scenario to a different target language community context — explaining what changed and why
Create an adaptation designed for a genuinely different audience (younger learners, community members) — reflect on what language adjustments were needed

response_modes.reason: Text adaptation skills develop through working with varied text types and adaptation conditions. Each new adaptation context requires different creative and linguistic decisions.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Adapting texts for real audiences and cultural contexts is where creative language use becomes genuinely purposeful — students are not copying but constructing something new for a real communicative purpose.
success_criteria: Produces a text adaptation with at least two changed elements suited to a different purpose
The adapted text is coherent and appropriate for the intended new audience or purpose
